rationales: NaCl solubility changes only slightly with temperature and is not the best answer.
Ce₂(SO₄)₃ becomes less soluble as temperature rises.
Li₂SO₄ does not show the marked increase in solubility expected here.
NaNO₃ solubility increases substantially as temperature rises.
Transition elements are metals, so they generally do not form ionic compounds with other metals.
Halogens gain electrons from metals to form ionic compounds.
Noble gases are generally unreactive and do not commonly form ionic compounds with metals.
Metalloids are not the usual partners for ionic compounds formed by metals.
At constant pressure, increasing temperature generally decreases gas density.
Increasing pressure compresses a gas and increases its density when temperature is fixed.
Constant volume alone does not specify a change that increases density.
Constant pressure alone does not specify a change that increases density.
Milk is a colloid and is classified as a heterogeneous mixture.
Ink may be a homogeneous solution or a colloidal mixture, depending on its composition.
Milk of magnesia is a suspension and is a heterogeneous mixture.
Sugar solution is homogeneous when the sugar is fully dissolved.
Gas in solid describes a mixture such as hydrogen dissolved in a metal, not dust in air.
Dust particles are solid particles dispersed in a gas.
Solid in liquid describes mixtures such as a suspension of sand in water.
Liquid in solid describes mixtures such as gels or certain solidified emulsions.
486 kJ/mol is not the accepted first ionization energy of sodium.
Sodium’s first ionization energy is approximately 496 kJ/mol.
738 kJ/mol is much higher than sodium’s first ionization energy.
590 kJ/mol is not the accepted first ionization energy of sodium.
9 is not the atomic number of carbon.
8 is the atomic number of oxygen, not carbon.
7 is the atomic number of nitrogen, not carbon.
Carbon has atomic number 6.
A cation has a positive charge.
An atom is electrically neutral when it has equal numbers of protons and electrons.
An anion is an ion with a negative charge.
A radical is a species with an unpaired electron and is not defined simply by a negative charge.
The first shell can hold a maximum of 2 electrons.
The second shell can hold a maximum of 8 electrons.
The M shell is the third shell and can hold a maximum of 18 electrons.
The fourth shell can hold a maximum of 32 electrons.
Horizontal rows in the modern periodic table are called periods.
Vertical columns, not horizontal rows, are called groups.
Noble gases are an element family, not the name for rows.
Transition elements are a category of elements, not the name for rows.
Ice is less dense, not denser, than liquid water.
Crystalline structure helps explain ice’s lower density but is not the direct comparison asked for.
Water is denser than ice, so ice floats on it.
Random molecular motion does not explain why ice floats.
Brick red is associated with calcium, not sodium.
Brilliant white is not the characteristic sodium flame colour.
Brilliant yellow is a common description of sodium’s flame colour.
Golden yellow is also a common description of sodium’s flame colour, making this option equivalent to brilliant yellow.
CH₄ contains only single covalent bonds.
C₂H₄ contains a carbon–carbon double bond.
C₂H₂ contains a carbon–carbon triple bond.
C₆H₆ is commonly represented with delocalized bonds and does not contain a carbon–carbon triple bond.
Air is generally a homogeneous mixture of gases.
Rock is heterogeneous because its composition and components vary.
Ice cream is a colloidal, heterogeneous mixture.
Gasoline is generally a homogeneous mixture of hydrocarbons.
Protons and electrons do not determine mass number; electrons are not counted in it.
Neutrons and electrons do not determine mass number.
Mass number is the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Protons alone give the atomic number, not the mass number.
